The prompt requests all five required descriptions of the code.

The prompt excludes prior-art research and requests no such report section.
Successful passes replace the single flat exploration.md file.

Implement and assist goldens cover report presence and absence.

work.explore.enabled defaults to true when its group or key is absent.
The config switch disables automatic passes without disabling manual exploration.
Agent and CLI precedence exist, but no configured exploration effort is read; effort falls back to heavy.
Automatic exploration skips human-completed sets.
Report reuse does not compare its recorded tree with the checkout.
Whole-drain tests cover missing and existing reports and assert whether exploration ran.
Failed attempts use the shared retry schedule and standard cap.
Failed exploration without a report produces EXPLORE-FAILED and stops the drain.
The park derives from captured runs and report absence without new store fields.
EXPLORE-FAILED remains separate from BLOCKED.
Automatic selection and daemon selection exclude parked sets.
Manual failures can create a park without progress; repeated drains with exploration disabled can append duplicate park records.
The skip flag bypasses exploration and its drain gate.
A successful manual report or removal of the declaration clears the park.
CONTEXT.md includes EXPLORE-FAILED in both required status lists.
ExploreMarkBadgeText hides the exploration mark beside EXPLORE-FAILED instead of retaining it with separate reason detail.
Undeclared sets carry no exploration mark, including after manual exploration.
Refresh resolves the exploration result and supplies the shared display surfaces.
Dashboard detail shows the report path and recorded tree without its body.
The sign-off preamble includes exploration beside the refine report.

scores.rationale: Good reuse and broad tests, but command coverage, configured effort, park records, and failed-state mark display remain incomplete.

accepted.behaviour: Tests drive the whole explore path together: the command, the agent reply, the report on disk and the captured run row, not each piece separately.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 02 criteria) says that tests drive the whole path, starting at the command. The Reference tests start at `exploreResolvedSet` and never run `pop tasks explore`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: The manifest's `explorer` object overrides the configured agent list and effort for the explore pass, and CLI flags override the `explorer` object.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 04 criteria) says that the `explorer` object overrides the configured agent list and the configured effort. The Reference has no configured Explorer effort: `resolveExplorer` falls back to `DefaultExploreEffort`. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.

accepted.behaviour: When a set parks, exactly one set-level progress record is added. It names the explore phase and the reason.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 05 criteria) says that the park appends exactly one set-level progress record. In the Reference, only the drain's `parkUnexplored` writes the record. A failed hand-run pass parks the set with no record, and repeated drains append one record each time. The spec wins; this is a defect in the Reference.

accepted.behaviour: A set that declared `explore` and has no report shows an exploration mark beside its status. The reason (not yet run, or the pass failed) appears as detail beside the mark, not inside the mark's value.
accepted.reason: The spec (task 06 criteria) says that a declared set with no report carries the mark beside its status, with the reason "the pass failed" as detail. In the Reference, `ExploreMarkBadgeText` returns an empty mark for a parked set. The spec wins; the Reference misses this behaviour.
